correctness.rationale: For Markov operators C(Y)->C(X), variation of each fiber measure gives norm 2(1-inf_x overlap). A continuous map X->Y lands in one connected covering component. Degree-one components admit unique inverse covering sections; nontrivial connected degree>=2 component admits no section by the clopen image argument. For any two maps involving a nontrivial component, pick a fiber miss of one: the other can overlap at most one atom, bounded by max(t1,u). For two degree-one maps overlap bounded by t1+t2 or by the equal-weight capped expression. Two-map continuous coverage construction uses a fixed sheet on alternating transition subintervals to connect arbitrary vertex lifts in connected Y_i; at least one of two maps is a sheet section locally at every edge position. This attains u with equal weights. The degree-one sections attain the other maxima. Independent exact rational examples verify the corollary: masses (3/4,1/4-epsilon,epsilon), degrees (1,1,2) yield errors 2epsilon and 1/2 for epsilon=.1,.01,.001. Frozen verify_examples.py only checks arithmetic, not the topological gluing.
